LESSON: CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.6: Conversational skills
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Conversational skills, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 8 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: How should one interrupt a speaker in a conversation without sounding rude?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify vocabulary related to foodstuff for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Conversational skills in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply etiquette and turn- taking skills in oral conversations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Conversational skills in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the place of etiquette in effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Conversational skills in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify vocabulary related to foodstuff for comprehension,

   Conversational skills helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. apply etiquette and turn- taking skills in oral conversations,

   Conversational skills helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. acknowledge the place of etiquette in effective communication.

   Conversational skills helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to a conversation about the kitchen, meal preparation and utensils used,

2. identify new words in a text related to the theme and pronounce them correctly,

3. collaborate with peers to talk about vocabulary related to kitchen items and meals, using simple descriptions,

4. work with peers to identify words used to interrupt a conversation politely,

5. engage in a dialogue using appropriate turn-taking skills and interrupting politely.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to a conversation about the kitchen, meal preparation and utensils used,
2. identify new words in a text related to the theme and pronounce them correctly,
3. collaborate with peers to talk about vocabulary related to kitchen items and meals, using simple descriptions,
4. work with peers to identify words used to interrupt a conversation politely,
5. engage in a dialogue using appropriate turn-taking skills and interrupting politely.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Conversational skills together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: These are enhanced as the learner speaks engagingly when collaborating with peers to

talk about vocabulary related to kitchen items and meals.

• Citizenship: This is enhanced as the learner demonstrates tolerance when engaging in a dialogue using appropriate turn

taking skills and interrupting politely.

12

Values:
• Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner diligently takes up assigned roles when engaging in a dialogue using

appropriate turn-taking skills and interrupting politely.

• Unity: This is enhanced as the learner works with peers to identify words used to interrupt a conversation politely

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Lifestyle diseases: This is addressed as the learner engages in discussions and texts on foods and drinks.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept on food and drinks to similar concepts on meals as taught in Agriculture.

1. identify vocabulary related to foodstuff for comprehension,
